nodes.statement_short: Under additive perturbation E, the optimal objective degrades by at most 2||E||_F^2.
nodes.label: thm:stability

nodes.name: Objective stable, variables not
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:sfmable} shows that the objective function value of Soft $k$-Means is stable and up to a constant factor of the oracle difference $\|\mathbf{E}\|_F^2$. This is definitely a good news. But for the variables, that is prototype $\mathbf{F}$ and membership $\mathbf{G}$, we cannot expect such a upper bound. Indeed, even for unperturbed data, we can prove a lower bound on the distance between a solution of Problem \eqref{thm:mainRes} and the oracle membership $\mathbf{G}^*$.
nodes.statement_short: The objective value is stable but the optimal F and G are not; a lower bound on G's distance to the oracle holds.

nodes.name: Lower bound (solution non-uniqueness)
nodes.statement: Let the best $(k-1)$-rank approximation of $\mathbf{X}$ be $\mathbf{X}_{k-1}$. For any oracle $\mathbf{G}^*$, there exists $\mathbf{G}$, which is a solution of Problem \eqref{eq:SfM}, such that \[ \|\mathbf{G} - \mathbf{G}^*\|_F^2 \geq \frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \| \mathbf{X}_{k-1}\|_F^2. \]
also_stated_at: Let the best $(k-1)$-rank approximation of $\mathbf{X}$ be $\mathbf{X}_{k-1}$. For any oracle $\mathbf{G}^*$, there exists $\mathbf{G}$, which is a solution of Problem \eqref{eq:SfM}, such that \[ \|\mathbf{G} - \mathbf{G}^*\|_F^2 \geq \frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \| \mathbf{X}_{k-1}\|_F^2. \]
assumptions: Let the best $(k-1)$-rank approximation of $\mathbf{X}$ be $\mathbf{X}_{k-1}$.
conclusions: there exists $\mathbf{G}$, which is a solution of Problem \eqref{eq:SfM}, such that \[ \|\mathbf{G} - \mathbf{G}^*\|_F^2 \geq \frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \| \mathbf{X}_{k-1}\|_F^2. \]
nodes.statement_short: Some optimal G is far from any oracle membership, by an amount proportional to ||X_{k-1}||_F^2.

nodes.name: Cause of non-uniqueness: unbounded prototype volume
nodes.statement: The solutions non-uniqueness issue is mainly caused since the volume\footnote{We abuse the notion volume here to refer to the volume relative to the affine subspace.} of the polyhedron of $\mathbf{F}$ can be made infinitely large to minimize the Problem \eqref{eq:add_constraint_G} in the affine span of $\mathbf{F}$,. We note that this issue has been realized in \cite{nascimento2003modeling} by arguing that for any $\alpha > 0$, $\alpha\mathbf{f}_i \cdot \frac{1}{\alpha} g_{ij}$ remain unchanged. Thus $\|\mathbf{f}_i\|$ can tend to infinity without change the objective value. In the next subsection, we try to address this issue by jointly minimizing the objective function of Soft $k$-Means and the volume of the $\mathbf{F}$ polyhedron.
nodes.statement_short: Non-uniqueness arises because the prototype simplex can be enlarged arbitrarily without changing the objective.

nodes.name: Centered data
nodes.statement: For simplicity, in this subsection, we assume the data is centered, that is, $\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n = 0$.

nodes.name: Volume of prototype polyhedron in span(U)
nodes.statement:
The volume of polyhedron generated by column vector of $\mathbf{F}$ in subspace $\text{span}(\mathbf{U})$ can be written as
\[
\text{vol}_{\text{span}(\mathbf{U})}(\mathbf{F}) = \frac{1}{(k-1)!} \det 
\left[ \begin{array}{c}
\mathbf{\Sigma V}^\top \\ \mathbb{1}_k^\top \end{array} 
\right]
\]
nodes.statement_short: Volume of the prototype simplex inside span(U), as a determinant of [Sigma V^T; 1^T] over (k-1)!.

nodes.name: Volume-regularized Soft k-Means (log-det form)
nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality, we minimize it within $\log$ and absorb the $1/(k-1)!$ into a hyper-parameter $\lambda$. The problem we concern is
\[
\min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 + \lambda \log \det 
\left[ \begin{array}{c}
\mathbf{\Sigma V}^\top \\ \mathbb{1}_k^\top \end{array}
\right].
\]
nodes.statement_short: Soft k-Means objective plus lambda times log-volume of the prototype simplex.

nodes.name: Log-det of volume matrix equals sum of log singular values
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{U\Sigma V}^\top$ such that $\mathbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k = 0$. Then, \[ \log \det \left[ \begin{array}{c} \mathbf{\Sigma V}^\top \\ \mathbb{1}_k^\top \end{array} \right] = \log(\sqrt{k}) + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log(\sigma_i(\mathbf{F})). \]
also_stated_at: Assume $\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{U\Sigma V}^\top$ such that $\mathbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k = 0$. Then, \[ \log \det \left[ \begin{array}{c} \mathbf{\Sigma V}^\top \\ \mathbb{1}_k^\top \end{array} \right] = \log(\sqrt{k}) + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log(\sigma_i(\mathbf{F})). \]
nodes.statement_short: For centered prototypes, the log-volume equals log sqrt(k) plus the sum of log singular values of F.

nodes.name: Log-singular-value regularized Soft k-Means
nodes.statement:
Using $\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n = 0$, we can see from \Cref{sec:proofSketch} that the condition $\mathbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k = 0$ satisfied,
which leads to a possible interesting problem
\[
\min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 + \frac{\lambda}{2} \sum_{i=1}^k \log(\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F})).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Soft k-Means plus (lambda/2) sum of log squared singular values of F (unbounded below).

nodes.name: Minimal Volume Soft k-Means (MVSkM)
nodes.statement_short: MVSkM: Soft k-Means plus (lambda/2) sum log(sigma_i^2(F)+eps), penalizing prototype-simplex volume.

nodes.name: MVSkM objective (7)
nodes.statement: \min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 + \frac{\lambda}{2} \sum_{i=1}^k \log(\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F}) + \varepsilon).
nodes.label: eq:mvsfm

nodes.name: MVSkM iteratively re-weighted alternating minimization (Algorithm 2)
nodes.statement: \caption{Solve the MVS$k$M Problem} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \Require $\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}$, $\lambda$, and the clusters number $k$ \State $\mathbf{F}_0 \leftarrow$ random initialized prototypes. \Repeat \State $\mathbf{V}_t \leftarrow$ left SV of $\mathbf{F}_t$ \State $\mathbf{D}_t \leftarrow\mathbf{V}_t \text{diag}(\{ 1/(\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F}_t) + \varepsilon) \}_{i=1}^k) \mathbf{V}_t^\top$ \State $\mathbf{F}_{t+1} \leftarrow \mathbf{X}\mathbf{G}_t(\mathbf{G}_t^\top\mathbf{G}_t + \lambda \mathbf{D}_t)^{-1}$ \State $\displaystyle \mathbf{G}_{t+1} \leftarrow \mathop{\arg\min}_{\mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}^\top\|_F^2.$ \Until{converge} \Ensure Prototypes $\mathbf{F} \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times c}$, membership $\mathbf{G} \in \mathbb{R}^{c \times n}$. \end{algorithmic}
also_stated_at:
Inspired by recent research on multi-task learning \cite{nie2018calibrated}, we design an iteratively re-weighted strategy  by performing alternating minimization on $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{G}$. Specifically, we update $\mathbf{F}_{t+1}$ by solving 
\[
\mathbf{F}_{t+1} = \mathop{\arg\min}_{F} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}\mathbf{G}_t^\top \|^2_F + \lambda \text{Tr}\left(\mathbf{D}_t\mathbf{F}^\top\mathbf{F}\right),
\]
where $\mathbf{D} = \mathbf{V}_t \text{diag}\left( \{ 1/(\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F}_t)+\varepsilon)  \}_{i=1}^{k} \right)$ and $\mathbf{F}_t = \mathbf{U}_t\mathbf{\Sigma}_t\mathbf{V}^\top$. Above subproblem for $\mathbf{F}$ can be solve easily using first-order optimal condition. Then, we update $\mathbf{G}_{t+1}$, by solve following $n$ problem
\[
(\mathbf{g}_i)_t = \mathop{\arg\min}_{\mathbf{g}\mathbb{1}_k = 1, \mathbf{g} \succeq 0} \| \mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{g}^\top \|_2^2,
\]
which is convex and can be solved with Projected Gradient Descent or even with Nesterov's acceleration.
nodes.statement_short: Alternate a re-weighted ridge-type closed-form F update with a simplex-constrained least-squares G update until convergence.
nodes.label: alg:MVSfM

nodes.name: Initialize F
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{F}_0 \leftarrow$ random initialized prototypes.
nodes.statement_short: Random prototype initialization.

nodes.name: Repeat loop
nodes.statement:
\Repeat
		\State $\mathbf{V}_t \leftarrow$ left SV of $\mathbf{F}_t$
		\State $\mathbf{D}_t \leftarrow\mathbf{V}_t \text{diag}(\{ 1/(\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F}_t) + \varepsilon) \}_{i=1}^k) \mathbf{V}_t^\top$
		\State $\mathbf{F}_{t+1} \leftarrow \mathbf{X}\mathbf{G}_t(\mathbf{G}_t^\top\mathbf{G}_t + \lambda \mathbf{D}_t)^{-1}$
		\State $\displaystyle \mathbf{G}_{t+1} \leftarrow \mathop{\arg\min}_{\mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}^\top\|_F^2.$
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the re-weighted updates.

nodes.name: Singular vectors of F_t
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{V}_t \leftarrow$ left SV of $\mathbf{F}_t$
nodes.statement_short: Singular vectors of the current prototypes.

nodes.name: Re-weighting matrix D_t
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{D}_t \leftarrow\mathbf{V}_t \text{diag}(\{ 1/(\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F}_t) + \varepsilon) \}_{i=1}^k) \mathbf{V}_t^\top$
nodes.statement_short: Re-weighting matrix from current singular values.

nodes.name: Update F
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{F}_{t+1} \leftarrow \mathbf{X}\mathbf{G}_t(\mathbf{G}_t^\top\mathbf{G}_t + \lambda \mathbf{D}_t)^{-1}$
nodes.statement_short: Closed-form re-weighted F update.

nodes.name: Update G
nodes.statement: $\displaystyle \mathbf{G}_{t+1} \leftarrow \mathop{\arg\min}_{\mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}^\top\|_F^2.$
nodes.statement_short: Simplex-constrained least-squares G update.

nodes.name: Convergence test
nodes.statement: \Until{converge}
nodes.statement_short: Stop at convergence.

nodes.name: MVSkM objective L(F,G)
nodes.statement:
For ease of notation, we shall write the objective function as
\[
\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}, \mathbf{G})=\| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}\mathbf{G}^\top\|_F^2 + \frac{\lambda}{2} \sum_{i=1}^k \log(\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F}) + \varepsilon).
\]

nodes.name: Descent of Algorithm 2
nodes.statement: Algorithm \ref{alg:MVSfM} is a descent method, that is, \[ \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t+1}, \mathbf{G}_{t+1}) \leq \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t}, \mathbf{G}_{t}). \]
also_stated_at: Algorithm \ref{alg:MVSfM} is a descent method, that is, \[ \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t+1}, \mathbf{G}_{t+1}) \leq \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t}, \mathbf{G}_{t}). \]
conclusions: Algorithm \ref{alg:MVSfM} is a descent method, that is, \[ \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t+1}, \mathbf{G}_{t+1}) \leq \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t}, \mathbf{G}_{t}). \]
nodes.label: thm:mvsfmDescent

nodes.name: Convergence of Algorithm 2
nodes.statement: Since the objective function (after $\varepsilon$ modification) of Problem \eqref{eq:mvsfm} is bounded from below ($\log(\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F}) + \varepsilon) \geq \log(\varepsilon)$), the iterative scheme will finally converge from Theorem \ref{thm:mvsfmDescent}.
assumptions: the objective function (after $\varepsilon$ modification) of Problem \eqref{eq:mvsfm} is bounded from below
conclusions: the iterative scheme will finally converge

nodes.name: k-LSDable
nodes.statement: Similarity matrix $\mathbf{K} \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is $k$-LSDable if $\exists c \in \mathbb{R}, \mathbf{G} \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}: \mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n$ such that $\mathbf{K} = \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{GG}^\top$.
nodes.statement_short: K is k-LSDable if K = (1/c) G G^T for a nonnegative row-stochastic G.

nodes.name: LSD optimum is a Soft k-Means optimum (Arora et al.)
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ is $k$-LSDable. Then the optimal $\mathbf{G}$ in LSD problem is also an optimum in the soft $k$-Means problem of $\mathbf{X}$.
conclusions: the optimal $\mathbf{G}$ in LSD problem is also an optimum in the soft $k$-Means problem of $\mathbf{X}$.
nodes.label: thm:jmlr13prop

nodes.name: LSDable implies SkMable
nodes.statement:
Above theorem indicates that if $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ is LSDable then it is S$k$Mable, which means that
\{LSDable\} $\subseteq$ \{S$k$Mable\}.

nodes.name: Translation invariant set K(X)
nodes.statement:
Define 
	\[
	\mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X}) = \left\{ \left( \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top  \right)^\top \left( \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right) : \mathbf{t}\in\mathbb{R}^d \right\}.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: K(X): Gram matrices of all translates X + t 1^T of the data.

nodes.name: Translation Invariant LSDable (TI-LSDable)
nodes.statement:
We say $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ is Translation Invariant LSDable (TI-LSDable) if there exists
	$
	\mathbf{K}^\prime \in \mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X})
	$ such that $\mathbf{K}^\prime$ is LSDable.
differentia: there exists $ \mathbf{K}^\prime \in \mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X}) $ such that $\mathbf{K}^\prime$ is LSDable
nodes.statement_short: K = X^T X is TI-LSDable if some translate's Gram matrix in K(X) is LSDable.

nodes.name: LSDable subset TI-LSDable subset SkMable
nodes.statement:
Indeed, one can easily see 
\[
\{\text{LSDable}\} \subseteq \{\text{TI-LSDable}\} \subseteq \{\text{S$k$Mable}\},
\]
where the first subset notation holds since that if $\mathbf{K}$ is LSDable, it must be TI-LSDable 
and the second one holds from the fact that if $\mathbf{X}$ is S$k$Mable then $\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top$ is also S$k$Mable..

nodes.name: Translation Invariant LSD (TI-LSD) problem
nodes.statement_short: Fit the closest Gram matrix of a translate of X by (1/c) G^T G with feasible G.

nodes.name: TI-LSD problem (8)
nodes.statement: \min_{\substack{c,\mathbf{G}\succeq 0, \mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n \\ \mathbf{K}^\prime \in \mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X}) } } \| \mathbf{K}^\prime - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \|_F^2
nodes.label: eq:TILSD

nodes.name: Relation between LSD of unLSDable Gram and Soft k-Means (Arora et al.)
nodes.statement:
The main result in this subsection is closely related to an open problem proposed in \cite{arora2013similarity},
in which it asked for the relation between LSD of unLSDable $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ and the solution of Soft $k$-Means for $\mathbf{X}$.
nodes.statement_short: Open question: how does the LSD solution of a non-LSDable X^T X relate to Soft k-Means on X?

nodes.name: Condition of TI-LSDable
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{K}$ is TI-LSDable if and only if rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$.
also_stated_at: $\mathbf{K}$ is TI-LSDable if and only if rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$.
conclusions: $\mathbf{K}$ is TI-LSDable if and only if rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$.
nodes.label: thm:TILSDable

nodes.name: SkMable is TI-LSDable
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$. $\mathbf{K}$ is TI-LSDable if and only if $\mathbf{X}$ is S$k$Mable.
conclusions: $\mathbf{K}$ is TI-LSDable if and only if $\mathbf{X}$ is S$k$Mable.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2
nodes.statement: Note that $\text{rank}(\mathbf{H}_n\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{XH}_n) = \text{rank}(\mathbf{XH}_n)$. For the if direction, since $\mathbf{X}$ is S$k$Mable, by Theorem \ref{thm:sfmable}, $\text{rank}(\mathbf{H}_n\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{XH}_n) = \text{rank}(\mathbf{XH}_n)\leq k-1$. For the only if direction, since $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ is TI-LSDable, by Theorem \ref{thm:TILSDable}, $\text{rank}(\mathbf{XH}_n) = \text{rank}(\mathbf{H}_n\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{XH}_n) \leq k-1$
nodes.statement_short: Use rank(H X^T X H) = rank(X H) and the rank characterizations of Theorems 2 and 7 in each direction.

nodes.name: Rank identity
nodes.statement: Note that $\text{rank}(\mathbf{H}_n\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{XH}_n) = \text{rank}(\mathbf{XH}_n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rank identity relating Gram and centered data.

nodes.name: If direction
nodes.statement: For the if direction, since $\mathbf{X}$ is S$k$Mable, by Theorem \ref{thm:sfmable}, $\text{rank}(\mathbf{H}_n\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{XH}_n) = \text{rank}(\mathbf{XH}_n)\leq k-1$.
nodes.statement_short: If: Theorem 2 gives the rank bound.

nodes.name: Only-if direction
nodes.statement:
For the only if direction, since $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ is TI-LSDable, by Theorem \ref{thm:TILSDable}, 
	$\text{rank}(\mathbf{XH}_n) = \text{rank}(\mathbf{H}_n\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{XH}_n) \leq k-1$
nodes.statement_short: Only if: Theorem 7 gives the rank bound.

nodes.name: TI-LSD solution is a Soft k-Means solution
nodes.statement: Assume kernel $\mathbf{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfies rank$(\mathbf{K}) \leq n-1$. If $\mathbf{G}^*$ is a solution of the TI-LSD in Problem \eqref{eq:TILSD} for kernel $\mathbf{K}$, then there exists $\mathbf{X}$ such that $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{G}^*$ is also a solution of S$k$M in Problem \eqref{eq:SfM}.
also_stated_at: Assume kernel $\mathbf{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfies rank$(\mathbf{K}) \leq n-1$. If $\mathbf{G}^*$ is a solution of the TI-LSD in Problem \eqref{eq:TILSD} for kernel $\mathbf{K}$, then there exists $\mathbf{X}$ such that $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{G}^*$ is also a solution of S$k$M in Problem \eqref{eq:SfM}.
assumptions: Assume kernel $\mathbf{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfies rank$(\mathbf{K}) \leq n-1$.
$\mathbf{G}^*$ is a solution of the TI-LSD in Problem \eqref{eq:TILSD} for kernel $\mathbf{K}$
conclusions: there exists $\mathbf{X}$ such that $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{G}^*$ is also a solution of S$k$M in Problem \eqref{eq:SfM}.
nodes.statement_short: A TI-LSD optimal membership for a rank-deficient kernel is also a Soft k-Means optimum for a factor X.
nodes.label: thm:tilsdEqual

nodes.name: Answer to the LSD/Soft k-Means open question
nodes.statement: In Theorem \ref{thm:tilsdEqual}, we show that for a given kernel $\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{XX}^\top$ satisfying rank$(\mathbf{K})\leq n-1$, its the optimal membership matrix for the LSD problem in Problem \eqref{eq:LSD} is still an optimal membership for the Soft $k$-Means problem on $\mathbf{X},$ which gives an answer for the relation between TI-LSD of unLSDable matrix $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ and the solution of soft $k$-Means for $\mathbf{X}$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 8 relates the TI-LSD solution of a non-LSDable Gram matrix to Soft k-Means, answering Arora et al.'s question.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (Condition of SkMable)
nodes.statement: For the {\em if} direction, choose $\textbf{F}$ and $\textbf{G}$ according to the Algorithm \ref{alg:global}. Directly calculation gives $\textbf{FG}^\top = \textbf{X}$. For the {\em only if} direction, note that \[ \textbf{X} - \frac{1}{k}\textbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_n^\top = \textbf{F}\left(\textbf{G}^\top - \frac{1}{k}\textbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top\textbf{G}^\top\right) = \textbf{FH}_k\textbf{G}. \] Using Lemma \ref{lem:rankXH}, we have \[ \begin{aligned} \text{rank}(\textbf{XH}_n) &\leq \text{rank}\left(\textbf{X} - \frac{1}{k}\textbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right)\\ &= \text{rank}\left(\textbf{F}\textbf{H}_k\textbf{G}^\top\right)\\ &\leq \text{rank}(\textbf{H}_k) \\ &= k-1. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: If: construct F, G by Algorithm 1. Only if: write the centered residual as F H_k G and bound its rank via Lemma 5.

nodes.name: If direction
nodes.statement:
For the {\em if} direction, choose $\textbf{F}$ and $\textbf{G}$ according to the Algorithm \ref{alg:global}. 
	Directly calculation gives $\textbf{FG}^\top = \textbf{X}$.
nodes.statement_short: If: Algorithm 1's F, G factor X exactly.

nodes.name: Only-if direction
nodes.statement:
For the {\em only if} direction, note that
	\[
	\textbf{X} - \frac{1}{k}\textbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_n^\top = \textbf{F}\left(\textbf{G}^\top - \frac{1}{k}\textbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top\textbf{G}^\top\right) = \textbf{FH}_k\textbf{G}.
	\]
	
	Using Lemma \ref{lem:rankXH}, we have
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\text{rank}(\textbf{XH}_n) &\leq \text{rank}\left(\textbf{X} - \frac{1}{k}\textbf{F}\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right)\\
	&= \text{rank}\left(\textbf{F}\textbf{H}_k\textbf{G}^\top\right)\\
	&\leq \text{rank}(\textbf{H}_k) \\
	&= k-1.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Only if: rank(XH_n) <= rank(F H_k G^T) <= k-1 via Lemma 5.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (Stability)
nodes.statement: Let $r_1 = $rank$(\textbf{X})$, $r_2 = $rank$(\widetilde{\textbf{X}})$, and $r_3 = $rank$(\textbf{E})$. Then $r = \max\{r_1, r_2, r_3\}.$ \[ \begin{aligned} \|\textbf{X} - \widetilde{\textbf{F}}_*\widetilde{\textbf{G}}_*^\top \|_F^2 =& \|\textbf{X} - \widetilde{\textbf{X}} + \widetilde{\textbf{X}} - \widetilde{\textbf{F}}_*\widetilde{\textbf{G}}_*^\top \|_F^2 \\ \leq& \|\textbf{X} - \widetilde{\textbf{X}} \|_F^2 + \| \widetilde{\textbf{X}} - \widetilde{\textbf{F}}_*\widetilde{\textbf{G}}_*^\top \|_F^2 \\ \leq& \|\textbf{E}\|_F^2 + \|\textbf{X} - \textbf{F}_*\textbf{G}_*^\top \|_F^2 + \sqrt{\sum_{i=k}^{r_2}\tilde{\sigma}_i^2} - \sqrt{\sum_{i=k}^{r_1}\sigma_i^2} \\ \overset{(a)}{\leq} & \|\textbf{E}\|_F^2 + \|\textbf{X} - \textbf{F}_*\textbf{G}_*^\top \|_F^2 + \sqrt{\sum_{i=k}^{r}\left(\tilde{\sigma}_i - \sigma_i\right)^2 } \\ \overset{(b)}{\leq}& 2\|\textbf{E}\|_F^2 + \|\textbf{X} - \textbf{F}_*\textbf{G}_*^\top \|_F^2, \end{aligned} \] where $(a)$ holds since $\|a\|-\|b\|\leq\|a-b\|$ and $(b)$ is from Mirsky's inequality (Lemma \ref{lem:mirsky}).
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality on the residual, then Mirsky's inequality bounds the change in tail singular values.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4 (Lower bound)
nodes.statement: Let \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb{A} &= \arg_{\mathbf{G}}\min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 \\ \mathbb{B} &= \left\{ \mathbf{G} \left| \mathbf{G}=\frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}}\mathbf{B}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}+\frac{1}{k}\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right.\right\}. \end{aligned} \] From Theorem \ref{thm:mainRes}, we know $\mathbb{A}\supseteq \mathbb{B}$. Indeed, for any $\mathbf{G}_1 \in \mathbb{B}$, exists $\mathbf{G}_2 \in \mathbb{B}$ such that \[ \begin{aligned} \|\mathbf{G}_1 - \mathbf{G}_2\|_F^2=&\left\| \frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}}\mathbf{B}\mathbf{R}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X} -\frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}}\mathbf{B}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X} \right\|_F^2 \\ =&\frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\| \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{R}-\mathbb{I})\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}\right\|_F^2 \\ =&\frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\|(\mathbf{R}-\mathbb{I})\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}\right\|_F^2 \\ \geq& \frac{2}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\|\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}\right\|_F^2 \\ =& \frac{2}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\|\mathbf{X}_{k-1}\right\|_F^2 \end{aligned} \] Note that \[ \begin{aligned} \max_{\mathbf{G}\in\mathbb{A}} \| \mathbf{G} - \mathbf{G}^* \|_F^2 \geq & \max_{\mathbf{G}\in\mathbb{B}} \| \mathbf{G} - \mathbf{G}^* \|_F^2 \\ \geq & \frac{1}{2}\left(\|\mathbf{G}_1 - \mathbf{G}^*\|_F + \|\mathbf{G}_2 - \mathbf{G}^*\|_F^2 \right) \\ \geq & \frac{1}{2} \|\mathbf{G}_1 - \mathbf{G}_2\|_F^2 \\ \geq & \frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\|\mathbf{X}_{k-1}\right\|_F^2, \end{aligned} \] which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Rotated solutions from Algorithm 1 are all optimal (Theorem 1) and pairwise far apart, so one is far from any oracle G*.

nodes.name: Define solution sets
nodes.statement:
Let
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\mathbb{A} &= \arg_{\mathbf{G}}\min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\succeq 0,\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 \\
	\mathbb{B} &= \left\{ \mathbf{G} \left|  \mathbf{G}=\frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}}\mathbf{B}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}+\frac{1}{k}\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right.\right\}.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	From Theorem \ref{thm:mainRes}, we know $\mathbb{A}\supseteq \mathbb{B}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the optimal set A and the rotated-solution family B; Theorem 1 gives A contains B.

nodes.name: Separate two solutions
nodes.statement:
Indeed, for any $\mathbf{G}_1 \in \mathbb{B}$, exists $\mathbf{G}_2 \in \mathbb{B}$ such that
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\|\mathbf{G}_1 - \mathbf{G}_2\|_F^2=&\left\| \frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}}\mathbf{B}\mathbf{R}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}
	-\frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}}\mathbf{B}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X} \right\|_F^2 \\
	=&\frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\| \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{R}-\mathbb{I})\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}\right\|_F^2 \\
	=&\frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\|(\mathbf{R}-\mathbb{I})\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}\right\|_F^2 \\
	\geq& \frac{2}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\|\mathbf{U}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{X}\right\|_F^2 \\
	=& \frac{2}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\|\mathbf{X}_{k-1}\right\|_F^2 
	\end{aligned}
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Two rotated solutions differ by at least a multiple of ||X_{k-1}||_F^2.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
Note that
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\max_{\mathbf{G}\in\mathbb{A}} \| \mathbf{G} - \mathbf{G}^* \|_F^2 
	\geq & \max_{\mathbf{G}\in\mathbb{B}} \| \mathbf{G} - \mathbf{G}^* \|_F^2 \\
	\geq & \frac{1}{2}\left(\|\mathbf{G}_1 - \mathbf{G}^*\|_F + \|\mathbf{G}_2 - \mathbf{G}^*\|_F^2 \right) \\
	\geq & \frac{1}{2} \|\mathbf{G}_1 - \mathbf{G}_2\|_F^2 \\ 
	\geq & \frac{1}{r\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \left\|\mathbf{X}_{k-1}\right\|_F^2,
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality: one of them is far from G*.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5 (Descent)
nodes.statement: Note that \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t+1}, \mathbf{G}_{t}) =&\|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}_t\|_F^2 +\lambda \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log(\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t+1})+\varepsilon) \\ =& \|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}_t\|_F^2 + \lambda(\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log(\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t+1})+\varepsilon) \\ &- \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log(\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon)) + \lambda\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log(\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon) \\ =& \|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}_t\|_F^2 +\lambda \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log( \frac{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t+1})+\varepsilon}{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon}) \\ &+ \lambda\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log(\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon) \\ \overset{(a)}{\leq}& \|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}_t\|_F^2 +\lambda \left( \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \frac{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t+1})}{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon} - \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \frac{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})}{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon}\right) \\ &+ \lambda\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log\left(\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})\right) \\ \overset{(b)}{\leq}& \|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}_t\|_F^2 +\lambda \text{Tr}(\mathbf{D}_t^\top \mathbf{F}_{t+1}^\top \mathbf{F}_{t+1}) - \lambda \text{Tr}(\mathbf{D}_t^\top \mathbf{F}_{t}^\top \mathbf{F}_{t}) \\ &+ \lambda\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log\left(\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t}+\varepsilon)\right) \\ \overset{(c)}{\leq}& \|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{F}_{t}\mathbf{G}_t\|_F^2 + \lambda\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \log\left(\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon\right) \\ =& \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t}, \mathbf{G}_{t}), \end{aligned} \] where (a) uses numerical inequality $\log(x)\leq x - 1$; (b) uses the asymmetric version of von Neumann's trace inequality (Lemma \ref{lem:traceIneq}) which implies $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t+1})}{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon} \leq \text{Tr}(\mathbf{D}_t^\top \mathbf{F}_{t+1}^\top \mathbf{F}_{t+1})$ and uses the definition of $\mathbf{D}_t$ which implies $\text{Tr}(\mathbf{D}_t^\top \mathbf{F}_{t}^\top \mathbf{F}_{t})=\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \frac{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})}{\sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{F}_{t})+\varepsilon}$; (c) uses $\|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{F}_{t+1}\mathbf{G}_t\|_F^2 +\lambda \text{Tr}(\mathbf{D}_t^\top \mathbf{F}_{t+1}^\top \mathbf{F}_{t+1})\leq \|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{F}_{t}\mathbf{G}_t\|_F^2 +\lambda \text{Tr}(\mathbf{D}_t^\top \mathbf{F}_{t}^\top \mathbf{F}_{t})$. Leveraging the definition of $\mathbf{G}_{t+1}$, it is easy to see $\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t+1}, \mathbf{G}_{t+1}) \leq \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{F}_{t+1}, \mathbf{G}_{t})$, which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Majorize the log terms by log x <= x - 1 and von Neumann's trace inequality; the F-step minimizes the majorizer and the G-step is exact.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7 (Condition of TI-LSDable)
nodes.statement: On the one hand, TI-LSDable $\Rightarrow$ rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$. The reason is that leveraging Theorem \ref{thm:jmlr13prop} we know if $\mathbf{K}$ is TI-LSDable, then $\mathbf{X}$ can be written as $\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{FG}^\top$. Thus, rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$. On the other hand, if rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$, then there exists $\mathbf{K}^\prime \in \mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X})$ such that $ \mathbf{K}^\prime = c_1\mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{P}$. We prove this claim as follows. Note that \[ \mathbf{F} = \mathbf{\bar{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top = r\sqrt{k(k-1)}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}\mathbf{B}^\top + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top. \] Then we have \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} &= \left( \bar{\mathbf{X}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right)^\top \left( \bar{\mathbf{X}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right) \\ &= \mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{F}^\top\mathbf{FP} \\ &= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)^\top \left( \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\ &= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top\bar{\mathbf{F}} + \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top + \mathbb{1}_k\mathbf{m}^\top \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P}. \end{aligned} \] According to rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathcal{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$, let $\mathbf{U}_\bot \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times (d-k+1)}$ be the orthocomplement of $\mathbf{U}_{k-1}$ and $\mathbf{m}=\mathbf{U}_\bot \mathbf{a}$ where $\mathbf{a} \in \mathbb{R}^{d-k+1}$. That is \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} &= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top\bar{\mathbf{F}} + \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top + \mathbb{1}_k\mathbf{m}^\top \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\ &= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top\bar{\mathbf{F}} + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\ &= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( r^2k(k-1)\mathbf{BU}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{U}_{k-1}\mathbf{B}^\top + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\ &= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( r^2k(k-1)\mathbf{B}\mathbf{B}^\top + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\ &= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( r^2k(k-1)\mathbb{I}_k - r^2(k-1) \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \end{aligned} \] Let $\|\mathbf{a}\|_2 = \|\mathbf{m}\|_2 = r\sqrt{k-1}$. Then we have \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} &= r^2k(k-1)\mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{P}, \end{aligned} \] which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Only if via Theorem 6 factorization; if: build F from Algorithm 1 with an orthogonal shift m of norm r*sqrt(k-1), making the Gram matrix a multiple of P^T P.

nodes.name: Only-if direction
nodes.statement: On the one hand, TI-LSDable $\Rightarrow$ rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$. The reason is that leveraging Theorem \ref{thm:jmlr13prop} we know if $\mathbf{K}$ is TI-LSDable, then $\mathbf{X}$ can be written as $\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{FG}^\top$. Thus, rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Only if: Theorem 6 gives X = F G^T, so the rank bound holds.

nodes.name: Expand Gram matrix
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, if rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$, then there exists $\mathbf{K}^\prime \in \mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X})$ such that $ \mathbf{K}^\prime = c_1\mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{P}$. We prove this claim as follows. Note that
	\[
	\mathbf{F} = \mathbf{\bar{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top = r\sqrt{k(k-1)}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}\mathbf{B}^\top + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top. 
	\]
	Then we have
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} &= \left( \bar{\mathbf{X}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right)^\top \left( \bar{\mathbf{X}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right) \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{F}^\top\mathbf{FP} \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)^\top \left( \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top\bar{\mathbf{F}} + \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top + \mathbb{1}_k\mathbf{m}^\top \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P}.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Write F as centered simplex plus shift m and expand X^T X.

nodes.name: If direction
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, if rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$, then there exists $\mathbf{K}^\prime \in \mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X})$ such that $ \mathbf{K}^\prime = c_1\mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{P}$. We prove this claim as follows. Note that
	\[
	\mathbf{F} = \mathbf{\bar{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top = r\sqrt{k(k-1)}\mathbf{U}_{k-1}\mathbf{B}^\top + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top. 
	\]
	Then we have
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} &= \left( \bar{\mathbf{X}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right)^\top \left( \bar{\mathbf{X}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right) \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{F}^\top\mathbf{FP} \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)^\top \left( \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top\bar{\mathbf{F}} + \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top + \mathbb{1}_k\mathbf{m}^\top \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P}.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	According to rank$(\mathbf{H}\mathcal{K}\mathbf{H}) \leq k-1$, let $\mathbf{U}_\bot \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times (d-k+1)}$ be the orthocomplement of $\mathbf{U}_{k-1}$ and $\mathbf{m}=\mathbf{U}_\bot \mathbf{a}$ where $\mathbf{a} \in \mathbb{R}^{d-k+1}$. That is
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} &= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top\bar{\mathbf{F}} + \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top \mathbf{m}\mathbb{1}_k^\top + \mathbb{1}_k\mathbf{m}^\top \bar{\mathbf{F}} + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( \bar{\mathbf{F}}^\top\bar{\mathbf{F}} + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( r^2k(k-1)\mathbf{BU}_{k-1}^\top\mathbf{U}_{k-1}\mathbf{B}^\top + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( r^2k(k-1)\mathbf{B}\mathbf{B}^\top + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P} \\
	&= \mathbf{P}^\top\left( r^2k(k-1)\mathbb{I}_k - r^2(k-1) \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top + \|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2 \mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{P}
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	Let $\|\mathbf{a}\|_2 = \|\mathbf{m}\|_2 =  r\sqrt{k-1}$. Then we have
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} &= r^2k(k-1)\mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{P},
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: If: construct a translate whose Gram matrix is LSDable.

nodes.name: Choose orthogonal shift
nodes.statement_short: Take m in the orthocomplement of U_{k-1}, killing cross terms.

nodes.name: Fix shift norm
nodes.statement:
Let $\|\mathbf{a}\|_2 = \|\mathbf{m}\|_2 =  r\sqrt{k-1}$. Then we have
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} &= r^2k(k-1)\mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{P},
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Choose ||m|| = r sqrt(k-1) so X^T X is proportional to P^T P.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{M}$ be some kernel that is TI-LSDable. Note that \[ \begin{aligned} &\|\mathbf{K} - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \|_F^2\\ =& \|\mathbf{K} - \mathbf{M} + \mathbf{M} - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \|_F^2 \\ = &\|\mathbf{K} - \mathbf{M} \|_F^2 + \|\mathbf{M} - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \|_F^2 + 2\langle \mathbf{K} - \mathbf{M}, \mathbf{M} - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \rangle. \end{aligned} \] Since we will optimize on $\mathbf{G}$ and $\mathbf{M}$ is LSDable, for any $\mathbf{M}$, we can choose $c$ and $\mathbf{G}$ such that $\mathbf{M}=\frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G}$. Thus the objective can be written as \[ \min_{\substack{\mathbf{K}\in\mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X}), \\ \mathbf{M} \text{ is LSDable} }}\|\mathbf{K} - \mathbf{M} \|_F^2. \] Assume $\mathbf{M} = \mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{Y}$. We always have $\mathbf{Y} = \overline{\mathbf{Y}} + \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top$, where $\mathbf{s} = \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{Y}\mathbb{1}_n$ and $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}\mathbb{1}_n = 0$. Using this decomposition, we rewrite above problem explicitly as \[ \min_{\substack{ \mathbf{t},\mathbf{s},\overline{\mathbf{Y}} \\ \mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{Y} \text{ is LSDable}}} \|(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)^\top(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top) - (\overline{\mathbf{Y}}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)^\top(\overline{\mathbf{Y}}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top) \|_F^2, \] where $\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n = 0$. Note that \[ \begin{aligned} &\|(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)^\top(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top) - (\overline{\mathbf{Y}}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)^\top(\overline{\mathbf{Y}}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top) \|_F^2 \\ =& \|(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}-\overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}}) + \mathbb{1}_n(\mathbf{t}^\top \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}}) + (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{t} - \overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\mathbf{s})\mathbb{1}^\top \\ &+ (\|\mathbf{t}\|^2 - \|\mathbf{s}\|^2)\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top \|_F^2 \\ =& \| \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}-\overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}} \|_F^2 + \| \mathbb{1}_n(\mathbf{t}^\top \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}}) + (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{t} - \overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\mathbf{s})\mathbb{1}^\top\\ &+ (\|\mathbf{t}\|^2 - \|\mathbf{s}\|^2)\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top \|_F^2 \\ =& \| \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}-\overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}} \|_F^2 + \| \mathbb{1}_n(\mathbf{t}^\top \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}}) + (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{t} - \overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\mathbf{s})\mathbb{1}^\top \|_F^2\\ &+ \|(\|\mathbf{t}\|^2 - \|\mathbf{s}\|^2)\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top \|_F^2, \end{aligned} \] where the second and third equality hold since $\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n=\overline{\mathbf{Y}}\mathbb{1}_n = 0$. From rank$(\mathbf{X})\leq n-1$ and rank$(\overline{\mathbf{Y}})\leq k-1$, we can alway choose proper $\mathbf{s}$ and $\mathbf{t}$ such that $\mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{Y}$ is LSDable and the second and third term are equal to zero. In detail, we choose $\|\mathbf{s}\|=\|\mathbf{t}\|$ and $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{t}=\overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\mathbf{s}=0$. Thus, the original problem becomes \[ \min_{\text{rank}(\overline{\mathbf{Y}})\leq k-1} \|(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} - \overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}} \|_F^2. \] The $(k-1)$-truncated SVD of $\mathbf{X}$ is a solution of above problem. Using Theorem \ref{thm:sfmable} and $\mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{Y} = \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}\mathbf{G}^\top$, the proof completes.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite TI-LSD as a nearest-LSDable-Gram problem, decouple translations via centering, and reduce to a rank-(k-1) approximation solved by truncated SVD and Theorem 2.

nodes.name: Introduce M
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{M}$ be some kernel that is TI-LSDable. Note that
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	&\|\mathbf{K} - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \|_F^2\\
	=& \|\mathbf{K} - \mathbf{M} + \mathbf{M} - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \|_F^2 \\
	= &\|\mathbf{K} - \mathbf{M} \|_F^2  + \|\mathbf{M} - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \|_F^2 + 2\langle \mathbf{K} - \mathbf{M}, \mathbf{M} - \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G} \rangle.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Insert an LSDable kernel M and expand the objective.

nodes.name: Reduce to nearest LSDable
nodes.statement:
Since we will optimize on $\mathbf{G}$ and $\mathbf{M}$ is LSDable, for any $\mathbf{M}$, we can choose $c$ and $\mathbf{G}$ such that $\mathbf{M}=\frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}^\top\mathbf{G}$. Thus the objective can be written as
	\[
	\min_{\substack{\mathbf{K}\in\mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X}), \\ \mathbf{M} \text{ is LSDable} }}\|\mathbf{K} - \mathbf{M} \|_F^2.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the distance from K(X) to the LSDable set.

nodes.name: Decompose Y
nodes.statement:
Assume $\mathbf{M} = \mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{Y}$. We always have $\mathbf{Y} = \overline{\mathbf{Y}} + \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top$, where $\mathbf{s} = \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{Y}\mathbb{1}_n$ and $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}\mathbb{1}_n = 0$. Using this decomposition, we rewrite above problem explicitly as
	\[
	\min_{\substack{ \mathbf{t},\mathbf{s},\overline{\mathbf{Y}} \\ \mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{Y} \text{ is LSDable}}} 
	\|(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)^\top(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top) - (\overline{\mathbf{Y}}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)^\top(\overline{\mathbf{Y}}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top) \|_F^2,
	\]
	where $\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose Y into centered part plus mean and rewrite the problem.

nodes.name: Split objective
nodes.statement:
Note that
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	&\|(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)^\top(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{t}\mathbb{1}_n^\top) - (\overline{\mathbf{Y}}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)^\top(\overline{\mathbf{Y}}+\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top) \|_F^2 \\
	=& \|(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}-\overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}}) + \mathbb{1}_n(\mathbf{t}^\top \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}}) + (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{t} - \overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\mathbf{s})\mathbb{1}^\top \\
	&+ (\|\mathbf{t}\|^2 - \|\mathbf{s}\|^2)\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top  \|_F^2 \\
	=& \| \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}-\overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}} \|_F^2 + \| \mathbb{1}_n(\mathbf{t}^\top \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}}) + (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{t} - \overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\mathbf{s})\mathbb{1}^\top\\
	&+ (\|\mathbf{t}\|^2 - \|\mathbf{s}\|^2)\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top \|_F^2 \\
	=& \| \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}-\overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}} \|_F^2 + \| \mathbb{1}_n(\mathbf{t}^\top \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}}) + (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{t} - \overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\mathbf{s})\mathbb{1}^\top \|_F^2\\
	&+ \|(\|\mathbf{t}\|^2 - \|\mathbf{s}\|^2)\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top \|_F^2,
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	where the second and third equality hold since $\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n=\overline{\mathbf{Y}}\mathbb{1}_n = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Orthogonality from centering splits the objective into three terms.

nodes.name: Eliminate translations
nodes.statement:
From rank$(\mathbf{X})\leq n-1$ and rank$(\overline{\mathbf{Y}})\leq k-1$, we can alway choose proper $\mathbf{s}$ and $\mathbf{t}$ such that $\mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{Y}$ is LSDable and the second and third term are equal to zero. In detail, we choose $\|\mathbf{s}\|=\|\mathbf{t}\|$ and $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{t}=\overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\mathbf{s}=0$. Thus, the original problem becomes
	\[
	\min_{\text{rank}(\overline{\mathbf{Y}})\leq k-1}  
	\|(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} - \overline{\mathbf{Y}}^\top\overline{\mathbf{Y}} \|_F^2.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose s, t to zero the cross terms, leaving a rank-(k-1) approximation problem.

nodes.name: Conclude via Theorem 2
nodes.statement: The $(k-1)$-truncated SVD of $\mathbf{X}$ is a solution of above problem. Using Theorem \ref{thm:sfmable} and $\mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{Y} = \frac{1}{c}\mathbf{G}\mathbf{G}^\top$, the proof completes.
nodes.statement_short: Truncated SVD solves it; conclude with Theorem 2.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Let $i_\infty$ be the index such that $x_{i_\infty} = \max_{1\leq i \leq k} |x_i|$. Note that \[ x_{i_\infty}^2 = \left( \sum_{i\neq i_\infty} x_i \right)^2 \leq (k-1)\sum_{i\neq i_\infty}x_i^2 \leq (k-1)(1-x_{i_\infty}^2), \] which indicates $x_{i_\infty}^2 \leq \frac{k-1}{k}$. The claim just follows.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz on the zero-sum constraint bounds the largest entry.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Note that, \[ \begin{aligned} \min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 &= \min_{\mathbf{s}, \mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \left( \mathbf{F}- \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{G}^\top\|_F^2\\ &\leq \min_{\substack{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n \\ \mathbf{s}, \text{rank}(F) \leq k-1 }} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top- \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2. \end{aligned} \] Assume that, \[ \mathbf{F}_*, \mathbf{G}_* = \mathop{\arg\min}_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n}\| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2. \] We have, \[ \begin{aligned} \left\|\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}_*\mathbf{G}_*^\top\right\|_F^2 &= \left\|\mathbf{X} - \left(\frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k\right)\mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{G}_*^\top - \left(\mathbf{F}_* - \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{G}_*^\top \right\|_F^2\\ &=\|\mathbf{X} - \hat{\mathbf{s}}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \hat{\mathbf{F}}\mathbf{G}_*^\top \|_F^2, \end{aligned} \] where $\hat{\mathbf{s}} := \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k, \hat{\mathbf{F}} := \mathbf{F}_* - \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top$. Note that $\hat{\mathbf{F}} \mathbb{1}_k = \mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k - \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top\mathbb{1}_k =\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k-\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k=0$. Thus, $\text{rank}(\hat{\mathbf{F}}) \leq k-1$ and we have \[ \begin{aligned} \min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 &= \left\|\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}_*\mathbf{G}_*^\top\right\|_F^2\\ &=\|\mathbf{X} - \hat{\mathbf{s}}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \hat{\mathbf{F}}\mathbf{G}_*^\top \|_F^2\\ &\geq\min_{\substack{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n \\ \mathbf{s}, \text{rank}(F) \leq k-1 }} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top- \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2, \end{aligned} \] which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Show both inequalities: translation gives <=, and recentering an optimal F yields a rank-(k-1) feasible point for >=.

nodes.name: One inequality
nodes.statement:
Note that,
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 
	&=
	\min_{\mathbf{s}, \mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \left( \mathbf{F}- \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{G}^\top\|_F^2\\
	&\leq
	\min_{\substack{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n \\ \mathbf{s}, \text{rank}(F) \leq k-1 }} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top- \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound via translation invariance.

nodes.name: Recenter optimum
nodes.statement:
Assume that,
	\[
	\mathbf{F}_*, \mathbf{G}_* = \mathop{\arg\min}_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n}\| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2.
	\]
	We have,
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\left\|\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}_*\mathbf{G}_*^\top\right\|_F^2
	&=
	\left\|\mathbf{X} - \left(\frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k\right)\mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{G}_*^\top - \left(\mathbf{F}_* - \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top \right)\mathbf{G}_*^\top  \right\|_F^2\\
	&=\|\mathbf{X} - \hat{\mathbf{s}}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \hat{\mathbf{F}}\mathbf{G}_*^\top  \|_F^2,
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	where $\hat{\mathbf{s}} := \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k, \hat{\mathbf{F}} := \mathbf{F}_* - \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top$.
nodes.statement_short: Recenter an optimal F_* into s-hat and F-hat.

nodes.name: Reverse inequality
nodes.statement:
Note that $\hat{\mathbf{F}} \mathbb{1}_k = \mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k - \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k\mathbb{1}_k^\top\mathbb{1}_k
	=\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k-\mathbf{F}_*\mathbb{1}_k=0$. Thus, $\text{rank}(\hat{\mathbf{F}}) \leq k-1$ and we have
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\min_{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 
	&=
	\left\|\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{F}_*\mathbf{G}_*^\top\right\|_F^2\\
	&=\|\mathbf{X} - \hat{\mathbf{s}}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \hat{\mathbf{F}}\mathbf{G}_*^\top  \|_F^2\\
	&\geq\min_{\substack{\mathbf{F},\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k = \mathbb{1}_n \\ \mathbf{s}, \text{rank}(F) \leq k-1 }} \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top- \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2,
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: F-hat has zero row sums, so rank <= k-1, giving the reverse inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Note that $\mathbf{F} = \mathbf{U}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^\top = \sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\sigma_i\mathbf{u}_i\mathbf{v}_i^\top$ and \[ \| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top- \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 = \sum_{i=1}^n \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{F}\mathbf{g}_i \|_2^2 \] Then we can write $\mathbf{g}_i = \mathbf{V}\mathbf{a}_i + \mathbf{v}_\bot b_i$, where $\mathbf{a}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{k-1}, b_i \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbf{v}_\bot \in \mathbb{R}^k,\mathbf{V}^\top\mathbf{v}_\bot=0$. We solve $\mathbf{g}_i$ by solving $\mathbf{a}_i$ and $b_i$. Note that \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{i=1}^n \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{F}\mathbf{g}_i \|_2^2 &= \sum_{i=1}^n \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{U}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^\top\mathbf{V}\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{U}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^\top \mathbf{v}_\bot b_i \|_2^2\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^n \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{U}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{a}_i\|_2^2. \end{aligned} \] Then we can obtain the optimal $\mathbf{a}_i$ as $\mathbf{a}_i^* = \mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s})$. Using the constraint $\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k=\mathbb{1}_n$, we have \[ \mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{g}_i = \mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{V}\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s}) + \mathbb{1}_k^\top\mathbf{v}_\bot b_i = 1, \] which gives the optimal $b_i$ as \[ b_i = \frac{1 - \mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{V}\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s})}{\mathbb{1}_k^\top\mathbf{v}_\bot }. \] Then the optimal $\mathbf{g}_i$ writes \[ \mathbf{g}_i^* = \mathbf{V} \mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s}) + \frac{1 - \mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{V}\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s})}{\mathbb{1}_k^\top\mathbf{v}_\bot } \mathbf{v}_\bot, \] which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose each g_i along V and v_perp; least squares fixes the V-part and the sum constraint fixes the v_perp coefficient.

nodes.name: Column-wise objective
nodes.statement:
Note that $\mathbf{F} = \mathbf{U}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^\top = \sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\sigma_i\mathbf{u}_i\mathbf{v}_i^\top$ and
	\[
	\| \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top- \mathbf{FG}^\top\|_F^2 
	= 
	\sum_{i=1}^n \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{F}\mathbf{g}_i \|_2^2
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Write the objective column-wise.

nodes.name: Parametrize g_i
nodes.statement:
Then we can write $\mathbf{g}_i = \mathbf{V}\mathbf{a}_i + \mathbf{v}_\bot b_i$, where $\mathbf{a}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{k-1}, b_i \in \mathbb{R}$ and 
	$\mathbf{v}_\bot \in \mathbb{R}^k,\mathbf{V}^\top\mathbf{v}_\bot=0$.  We solve $\mathbf{g}_i$ by solving $\mathbf{a}_i$ and $b_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize g_i = V a_i + v_perp b_i.

nodes.name: Solve a_i
nodes.statement:
Note that
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\sum_{i=1}^n \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{F}\mathbf{g}_i \|_2^2
	&=
	\sum_{i=1}^n \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{U}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^\top\mathbf{V}\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{U}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^\top \mathbf{v}_\bot b_i \|_2^2\\
	&=
	\sum_{i=1}^n \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{U}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{a}_i\|_2^2.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	Then we can obtain the optimal $\mathbf{a}_i$ as $\mathbf{a}_i^* = \mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s})$.
nodes.statement_short: v_perp drops out; least squares gives a_i.

nodes.name: Solve b_i
nodes.statement:
Using the constraint $\mathbf{G}\mathbb{1}_k=\mathbb{1}_n$, we have
	\[
	\mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{g}_i = \mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{V}\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s}) + \mathbb{1}_k^\top\mathbf{v}_\bot b_i = 1,
	\]
	which gives the optimal $b_i$ as
	\[
	b_i = \frac{1 - \mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{V}\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s})}{\mathbb{1}_k^\top\mathbf{v}_\bot }.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Sum-to-one constraint determines b_i.

nodes.name: Assemble g_i
nodes.statement:
Then the optimal $\mathbf{g}_i$ writes
	\[
	\mathbf{g}_i^* = \mathbf{V} \mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s}) +  \frac{1 - \mathbb{1}_k^\top \mathbf{V}\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}\mathbf{U}^\top(\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{s})}{\mathbb{1}_k^\top\mathbf{v}_\bot } \mathbf{v}_\bot,
	\]
	which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Assemble the optimal g_i.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Using $\det (\mathbf{A}\mathbf{A}^\top)= \det^2 \mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{V}^\top\mathbb{1}_k = 0$, we have \[ \begin{aligned} \log \det \left[ \begin{array}{c} \mathbf{\Sigma V}^\top \\ \mathbb{1}_k^\top \end{array} \right] =& \frac{1}{2} \log \det \left( \left[ \begin{array}{c} \mathbf{\Sigma V}^\top \\ \mathbb{1}_k^\top \end{array} \right] \left[ \begin{array}{c} \mathbf{\Sigma V}^\top \\ \mathbb{1}_k^\top \end{array} \right]^\top \right) \\ =& \frac{1}{2} \log \det \left( \left[ \begin{array}{c c} \mathbf{\Sigma}^2 & 0 \\ 0 & k \end{array} \right] \right) \\ =& \frac{1}{2}\log \left( k\prod_{i=1}^{k-1}\sigma_i^2(\mathbf{F}) \right) \\ =& \log\sqrt{k} + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\log \sigma_i(\mathbf{F}), \end{aligned} \] which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Use det(AA^T) = det(A)^2 and V^T 1 = 0 to block-diagonalize.

nodes.name: Centering minimizes rank over translations
nodes.statement: Given $\mathbf{s}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, we have rank$(\mathbf{XH}_n) \leq$ rank$(\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top)$.
nodes.label: lem:rankXH

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Leveraging the rank-sum inequality Lemma \ref{lem:rankSum}, we have \[ \text{rank}\left(\mathbf{X} - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right) \leq \text{rank}\left(\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right) + \text{rank}\left(\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right), \] where the equality holds only if $\text{range}\left( \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right) \cap \text{range}\left(\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right) = \{0\}$. Note that \[ \text{range}\left( \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right) \ni \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s}}{n} = \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n - \mathbf{s} \in \text{range}\left(\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right), \] which concludes that the equality cannot hold. Thus $ \text{rank}\left(\mathbf{XH}_n\right) < \text{rank}\left(\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right) + 1, $ which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the rank-sum inequality and show its equality case fails because the ranges intersect.

nodes.name: Apply rank-sum inequality
nodes.statement:
Leveraging the rank-sum inequality Lemma \ref{lem:rankSum}, we have
	\[
	\text{rank}\left(\mathbf{X} - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right)
	\leq \text{rank}\left(\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right) + \text{rank}\left(\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right),
	\]
	where the equality holds only if $\text{range}\left( \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right) \cap \text{range}\left(\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right) = \{0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Rank-sum inequality with its equality condition.

nodes.name: Strictness and conclude
nodes.statement:
Note that
	\[
	\text{range}\left( \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top \right) \ni \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{s}}{n} = \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n - \mathbf{s} \in \text{range}\left(\mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}\mathbb{1}_n\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right),
	\]
	which concludes that the equality cannot hold. Thus
	$
	\text{rank}\left(\mathbf{XH}_n\right)
	< \text{rank}\left(\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{s}\mathbb{1}_n^\top\right) + 1,
	$
	which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: The ranges share a nonzero vector, so the inequality is strict.

nodes.name: von Neumann's trace inequality (asymmetric version)
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $\mathbf{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ are symmetric. Then \[ \sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_{n-i+1}(\mathbf{A})\sigma_i(\mathbf{B}) \leq \text{Tr}(\mathbf{AB})\leq \sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_{i}(\mathbf{A})\sigma_i(\mathbf{B}). \]
assumptions: Assume $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $\mathbf{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ are symmetric.
nodes.label: lem:traceIneq

nodes.name: Rank-sum inequality
nodes.statement: The rank-sum inequality: If $\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B} \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, then \[ \text{rank}(\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B}) \leq \text{rank}(\mathbf{A}) + \text{rank}(\mathbf{B}), \] with equality {\em if and only if} $ (\text{range}\ \mathbf{A}) \cap (\text{range}\ \mathbf{B}) = \{0\}$ and $ (\text{range}\ \mathbf{A}^\top) \cap (\text{range}\ \mathbf{B}^\top) = \{0\}. $
nodes.label: lem:rankSum

nodes.name: Mirsky's inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$. Then \[ \sum_{i=1}^n \left(\sigma_i(\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{E}) - \sigma_i(\mathbf{A}) \right)^2 \leq \|\mathbf{E}\|_F^2. \]
nodes.label: lem:mirsky
